h1: Investor Renovation Contractor in Fort Lauderdale
intro:
Fort Lauderdale is a mid-century city at heart. Most of the houses and small apartment buildings investors buy here went up between the late 1940s and the 1960s, in concrete block on slabs, with flat or low-slope roofs, terrazzo floors and jalousie windows. On a dry lot in Lauderdale Manors that stock is straightforward to renovate. On a canal in Rio Vista or a low street in Edgewood or Riverland, the same house carries flood rules, seawall standards and a buyer who remembers the April 2023 rainstorm.

Genstone Construction renovates investment property across Fort Lauderdale for flippers, buy-and-hold landlords, owner-occupant buyers, lenders, servicers and funds. We are headquartered in Romeoville, Illinois and coordinate vetted, licensed Broward County contractors, with a designated field manager responsible for every job. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices the repairs, tests the after-repair value and puts hurricane-code, flood and permit costs on paper before your money is committed. There is no upfront payment, and draws are tied to completed work.
housingStock:
Fort Lauderdale's oldest surviving homes cluster around the New River. Sailboat Bend, a locally designated historic district, holds frame vernacular cottages, Mission and Mediterranean Revival houses from the 1910s through the 1930s, many raised slightly on piers. Croissant Park, Tarpon River and the edges of Rio Vista add 1920s and 1930s homes mixed with later infill.

The city's character, though, comes from the postwar boom. Victoria Park, Poinsettia Heights, Middle River Terrace and Lake Ridge filled with modest block cottages and, just as often, small multifamily: side-by-side duplexes, two-story walk-up apartment buildings with exterior stairs and catwalks, and courtyard buildings of four to a dozen units. Lauderdale Manors, Dorsey-Riverbend, Riverland, Edgewood and the neighborhoods west of I-95 are dominated by 1950s and 1960s block ranches on slabs. Many have Florida rooms, enclosed carports and later additions.

The canal neighborhoods, including Rio Vista, the Las Olas Isles, Harbor Beach and Coral Ridge, began with the same mid-century ranches, now steadily replaced by large new homes. A dated canal-front ranch is often priced as land, which changes the renovation calculation completely.

Common construction features across this stock include concrete block walls with tie beams, flat or low-slope roofs with built-up or modified bitumen membranes, cast-iron drains under slabs, terrazzo floors, aluminum awning or jalousie windows and electrical systems that predate modern loads.

For investors, the important variables are elevation and flood zone, roof type, the condition of concrete and drains and the legal status of additions or extra units. Two houses that look identical from the street can differ sharply on those points. Lead paint should be assumed in anything built before 1978, and asbestos turns up regularly in old floor tile, popcorn ceilings and roofing mastic from the 1950s through the 1970s, so testing belongs at the front of any scope that disturbs those materials.

commonIssues.title: Flat roofs and HVHZ re-roofing
commonIssues.body: Many Fort Lauderdale homes and small apartment buildings have flat or low-slope roofs with built-up or modified bitumen membranes. Ponding water, failed flashing at parapets and deteriorated decking are common. Broward County is in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so re-roofing must follow stricter attachment, underlayment and product approval rules. We inspect the deck and drainage, price HVHZ-compliant systems and include tapered insulation where ponding is a problem, so the new roof sheds water properly.

commonIssues.title: Cast-iron drains and slab plumbing
commonIssues.body: Cast-iron drain lines under slabs are nearly universal in Fort Lauderdale homes and apartment buildings built before the 1980s. In South Florida conditions they corrode from the inside, cracking and losing their bottoms. Symptoms include slow drains, backups and odors, but the real cost lies in cutting slabs or tunneling to replace them. We camera-inspect drains during the review because replacement can significantly affect the budget, especially in multifamily buildings with shared lines.

commonIssues.title: Flooding, king tides and seawalls
commonIssues.body: Low neighborhoods near the New River, the Middle River and the Intracoastal see tidal flooding during seasonal king tides, and the April 2023 rainstorm flooded Edgewood, Riverland and other areas far from the water. In Special Flood Hazard Areas, renovations reaching half the structure's value trigger substantial improvement requirements. Canal-front properties also face city seawall height standards when walls are built or substantially repaired. We check flood zone, history and seawall condition before scoping.

commonIssues.title: Unpermitted additions and units
commonIssues.body: Enclosed carports, Florida rooms built without permits, garage conversions and extra units added to duplexes are common in Fort Lauderdale. Unpermitted space may be excluded by appraisers, refused by insurers and flagged by buyers and lenders. Some extra units are rented informally and cannot be legalized under zoning. We compare property records with the actual layout and price legalization, conversion or removal before you rely on that space or income.

commonIssues.title: Concrete spalling and corrosion
commonIssues.body: Salt air and humidity corrode the rebar inside concrete tie beams, columns, balconies and exterior stairs, causing spalling. On mid-century walk-up apartment buildings with exterior catwalks, this can become a safety issue. Metal railings, window frames and fasteners corrode as well. Repairs involve cutting back to sound concrete, treating or replacing the steel and patching to specification, usually with permits. Painting over spalls only hides a problem that will grow.

investorMarket:
Fort Lauderdale strategies sort by location relative to water and by building type.

Flips perform best in neighborhoods where renovated mid-century homes set strong comps without being priced as teardowns: Victoria Park's single-family streets, Poinsettia Heights, Middle River Terrace, Croissant Park, Tarpon River and parts of Lake Ridge. Buyers there want impact windows, an updated roof, clean permit histories and modern kitchens and baths. In canal neighborhoods, a renovated ranch competes with new construction and land value, so the numbers need extra scrutiny.

Buy-and-hold and BRRRR investors often focus on block ranches in Lauderdale Manors, Dorsey-Riverbend, Riverland and neighborhoods west of I-95. These homes rent steadily and have renovated comparables, though flood exposure varies and should be checked property by property.

Small multifamily is a major part of the market. Victoria Park, Poinsettia Heights, Middle River Terrace and Lake Ridge have duplexes and walk-up buildings that produce strong rents. Many need roofs, concrete repair, drains, electrical upgrades and impact windows. Some investors convert units to furnished or short-term rentals, which requires following the city's vacation rental registration rules.

FHA 203(k) buyers often target duplexes they can live in and mid-century single-family homes needing systems work. REO properties appear across the city, with flood-affected and long-vacant homes forming a distinct segment. Wilton Manors and Oakland Park, just north, have similar housing but separate building departments.
permits:
Inside city limits, residential permits are issued by the City of Fort Lauderdale's Development Services Department through its building services division. Wilton Manors, Oakland Park, Plantation, Hollywood and the other Broward cities each run their own building departments, and the few remaining unincorporated pockets fall under Broward County.

Work requiring permits includes re-roofing, window and door replacement, shutters, electrical service and panel changes, rewiring, re-piping, HVAC and water heater replacement, structural and concrete repairs, seawall and dock work and any layout changes or legalization of additions. Broward is in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so roofing, windows, doors and shutters must carry the required product approvals and are inspected against them. Broward County's Board of Rules and Appeals adopts local amendments that apply countywide.

In flood zones, the city compares the cost of proposed work with the structure's value to determine whether substantial improvement requirements apply. Canal-front properties may need to meet seawall height standards when walls are built or substantially repaired. Sailboat Bend and Himmarshee are locally designated historic districts with exterior review. Larger multifamily buildings may fall under the county's building safety inspection program. A recorded Notice of Commencement and lien waivers are required for most permitted work. Genstone handles applications, inspections and documentation.
climate:
Fort Lauderdale's subtropical climate never brings freezes, but water and wind drive renovation decisions. The wet season brings intense afternoon storms and occasional extreme rainfall, as the April 2023 event showed. We schedule roofing, exterior painting and concrete work for the drier months when possible and close up openings early on any project running through hurricane season.

Salt air near the ocean, the Intracoastal and the canals corrodes metal fasteners, railings, HVAC coils and electrical components, so material choices must account for it. Stainless or coated hardware and corrosion-resistant equipment last longer.

King tides in the fall push water into low streets near the waterways, and high groundwater limits drainage. Humidity is constant, so homes closed without air conditioning grow mold quickly. HVAC systems must be sized for dehumidification, and roof and window details must keep water out of block walls.

faqs.q: Is a canal-front ranch in Fort Lauderdale worth renovating?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but compare it with the land value first. In Rio Vista, the Las Olas Isles and Coral Ridge, many mid-century ranches sell primarily for their lots, and builders replace them with new homes. A renovation makes sense when the house is sound, above flood requirements or within substantial improvement limits and the comps for renovated ranches support the cost. We run that comparison during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review, including seawall condition and height requirements.

faqs.q: Do I need impact windows on a Fort Lauderdale renovation?
faqs.a: Any replacement windows and doors must meet High-Velocity Hurricane Zone requirements, which in practice means impact-rated products or approved shutters. You are not always required to replace every opening, but buyers, insurers and lenders in Fort Lauderdale increasingly expect protection. Impact windows also improve wind mitigation credits. We price compliant options and compare their cost with the value and insurance benefits they bring for your specific property.

faqs.q: Did the April 2023 flood change how you scope Fort Lauderdale homes?
faqs.a: Yes. That storm flooded neighborhoods such as Edgewood and Riverland that many people did not consider high risk. We now check flood history, not just the flood zone, and look for signs of past water intrusion such as replaced lower drywall, stained baseboards or new flooring in an otherwise dated house. If a house flooded, we confirm that damaged materials were properly removed and the electrical and HVAC systems were evaluated.

faqs.q: Does Genstone have a local office in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: No. Our only office is our Romeoville, Illinois headquarters, and we do not pretend otherwise. In Fort Lauderdale, we coordinate a network of vetted, licensed and insured Broward County contractors under a designated field manager. That model combines local trades who know HVHZ products, flat roofs, concrete repair and city inspections with our estimating, scheduling and documentation. You can follow progress and milestones without visiting the property.

fix-flip.title: Fix and Flip Contractor in Fort Lauderdale, FL | Genstone
fix-flip.metaDescription: Fort Lauderdale fix and flip renovations for mid-century block homes: impact windows, flat-roof systems, permit cleanup, flood checks and buyer-ready finishes.
fix-flip.h1: Fix and Flip Renovations in Fort Lauderdale
fix-flip.intro: Fort Lauderdale buyers have seen a lot of flipped mid-century houses, and they have learned what to look for. They check whether the windows are impact-rated, whether the flat roof is new and properly sloped to drain, whether the drains under the slab were replaced and whether the Florida room shows up on the permit record. Since 2023 they also ask whether the house took water. Genstone scopes Fort Lauderdale flips to answer those questions before a buyer asks them, and then finishes the house to the level that renovated comps on the same streets support. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review covers all of it, including the flood check and the comparison between a renovation and a teardown sale for canal-front lots.

sections.h2: What Fort Lauderdale buyers check first
sections.body:
A Fort Lauderdale buyer's inspector will look closely at a few items that can make or break the sale. Windows and doors should meet High-Velocity Hurricane Zone standards, ideally impact-rated. The roof, often flat or low-slope on mid-century homes, should be new or recent, with proper drainage and current attachment. Drains under the slab should be camera-inspected, and original cast iron is a red flag. The electrical panel and wiring should be current.

Permits matter as much as condition. Enclosed carports, Florida rooms and converted garages are common, and if they do not appear on the permit record, appraisers may exclude them and insurers may refuse coverage. Open permits from previous owners also appear in lien searches.

We address these items early. The scope includes impact openings where comps support them, an HVHZ-compliant roof with tapered insulation for drainage, drain replacement where needed and permit cleanup for additions. At listing, your agent can provide a clean file, which keeps negotiations focused on price instead of repairs.

sections.h2: Renovation or teardown in canal neighborhoods
sections.body:
In Rio Vista, the Las Olas Isles and Coral Ridge, a mid-century ranch on a canal may be worth more as a lot than as a renovated house. Builders buy these properties, remove the house and build large new homes. A flip in these neighborhoods must compete with new construction and with the land value itself.

We compare the two paths during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review. If the house is structurally sound, sits at an acceptable elevation and renovated comps support the cost, a well-executed renovation can produce a strong return. If the house is low, the flood zone triggers substantial improvement limits or the seawall needs major work, the numbers often favor reselling as a lot or partnering with a builder.

Seawall condition deserves attention on every canal property. A deteriorating wall is expensive to replace, and the city's height standards apply when walls are built or substantially repaired. We include seawall evaluation in the review so the cost appears in your analysis rather than in the buyer's inspection.

sections.h2: Finishes and schedule for Fort Lauderdale comps
sections.body:
Mid-century homes in Victoria Park, Poinsettia Heights, Middle River Terrace and Croissant Park respond well to clean, modern renovations that respect their era. Polished terrazzo floors, open kitchens where walls allow, simple tile baths and good lighting tend to appeal to buyers. Outdoor living space matters here, so patios, pergolas and landscaping often deserve part of the budget.

We price finish options against renovated sales nearby and often provide two finish levels with estimated after-repair values. That lets you see which upgrades add value and which only add cost.

Scheduling follows the weather. Roofs, windows and doors go in early so the house is closed up during the wet season, with HVAC installed before flooring and cabinets. Permits and inspections run through the City of Fort Lauderdale or the relevant Broward city, and historic properties in Sailboat Bend need exterior review. Your field manager provides progress photos and milestone updates, and draws are tied to completed work.

faqs.q: Are impact windows necessary on a Fort Lauderdale flip?
faqs.a: In most neighborhoods where renovated comps have them, yes. Buyers in Victoria Park, Poinsettia Heights and similar areas expect hurricane protection, and impact windows improve insurance credits and appraisals. Further west, where price points are lower, accordion or panel shutters with the right approvals may stretch the budget further. We review nearby renovated sales to see what buyers are paying for, then price both options so you can choose the one that gives the better return.

faqs.q: How do flat roofs affect a Fort Lauderdale flip budget?
faqs.a: Significantly. Many mid-century homes have flat or low-slope roofs with ponding water, failed flashing at parapets and deteriorated decking. Replacement must meet High-Velocity Hurricane Zone requirements for attachment and products. We inspect the deck, check drainage and often include tapered insulation so the new roof sheds water properly. A new, permitted roof is also one of the first things buyers and insurers ask about.

faqs.q: Should I flip a canal-front ranch or sell it as a lot?
faqs.a: It depends on the house, the elevation, the flood zone, the seawall and the comps. If the house is sound and renovated comps support the cost, a renovation can work well. If the house is low, would trigger substantial improvement requirements or needs a new seawall, selling as a lot or partnering with a builder may produce a better return. We compare both paths during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review.

brrrr.title: BRRRR Rehab Contractor in Fort Lauderdale, FL | Genstone
brrrr.metaDescription: BRRRR rehabs in Fort Lauderdale: block ranches and legal duplexes renovated for the refinance appraisal, HVHZ wind credits, flood checks and long holds.
brrrr.intro: Fort Lauderdale rents can carry a BRRRR deal, but two costs decide whether the strategy works: insurance and flood exposure. A Lauderdale Manors ranch with an old flat roof, original jalousies and a panel insurers refuse can be nearly impossible to insure at a sensible price, while the same house with an HVHZ roof, impact openings and current systems can earn meaningful wind mitigation credits. Flood zones and the history of the April 2023 storm add another layer. Genstone scopes Fort Lauderdale BRRRR projects to reach the refinance value the comps support while bringing those carrying costs into line. We document every improvement for the appraiser and the insurer, and Genstone Financial can discuss DSCR rental loans for the refinance if you want to keep it in the same group.

sections.h2: Picking the right Fort Lauderdale BRRRR property
sections.body:
Fort Lauderdale's block ranches in Lauderdale Manors, Dorsey-Riverbend, Riverland and the neighborhoods west of I-95 are common BRRRR targets. They rent steadily and have renovated comparables. The variable is water. Some streets sit in Special Flood Hazard Areas, and others flooded in April 2023 despite being outside mapped zones. Flood insurance costs, substantial improvement limits and tenant disruption after a flood all affect the strategy.

We review each property's flood zone, elevation certificate if available and flood history. We also look for signs of past water damage that may have been covered up. That analysis helps you choose properties where flood exposure is manageable.

Legal duplexes in Poinsettia Heights, Middle River Terrace and Lake Ridge can also work well. Before counting rent from every unit, we confirm that each is recognized by the city. An informal third unit or converted garage will not count in a refinance appraisal and may create code and insurance problems.

sections.h2: Renovating for the appraisal and the insurer
sections.body:
An appraiser valuing a renovated Fort Lauderdale ranch or duplex compares it with nearby renovated properties and adjusts for condition, kitchens and baths, roof age, windows, HVAC and system updates. We set the scope to what the comps support, avoiding upgrades that add cost without raising the appraisal.

Insurance is equally important. Florida insurers price wind coverage partly on the wind mitigation inspection, which considers roof covering, deck attachment, roof-to-wall connections and opening protection. A new HVHZ roof with proper attachment, documented roof-to-wall connections and impact-rated or protected openings can earn credits. Four-point inspection items, including the roof, panel, plumbing and HVAC, must be in acceptable condition.

We document every upgrade with permits, product approvals and photos. That record helps the appraiser support the condition adjustments and gives your insurance agent what they need to present the property to carriers. The goal is a refinance that returns your capital and a premium the rent can comfortably support.

Fort Lauderdale tenants care most about air conditioning, followed by functional kitchens and baths, laundry and outdoor space. We size HVAC for dehumidification, clean or replace ducts, vent bath fans outdoors and install condensate lines with accessible cleanouts.

Materials should handle humidity and heavy use. Porcelain tile or polished terrazzo floors, solid-surface counters, moisture-resistant paint and fixtures with available parts reduce turn costs. Near the water, outdoor HVAC equipment, railings and fasteners should be corrosion-resistant.

In older block homes, original cast-iron drains should be replaced during the rehab rather than after a tenant moves in. Concrete spalling on tie beams or exterior stairs should be repaired before it becomes a safety issue.

Outdoor space earns its keep in this market too. A patio slab, a privacy fence and a shade structure cost little relative to the rent premium they support, and tenants in Lauderdale Manors or Riverland use them year-round.

At the finish line you hold a house ready to lease, appraise and insure, backed by a record of every improvement and a one-year workmanship warranty that excludes tenant damage and normal wear.

faqs.q: Which Fort Lauderdale areas suit BRRRR?
faqs.a: Block-ranch neighborhoods such as Lauderdale Manors, Dorsey-Riverbend, Riverland and the areas west of I-95 are common choices, along with legal duplexes in Poinsettia Heights, Middle River Terrace and Lake Ridge. Flood exposure varies street by street, so we check each property's flood zone, elevation and history. Legal unit count, insurance costs and renovated comps all factor into whether the strategy works on a specific property.

faqs.q: Can a renovation reduce insurance costs on a Fort Lauderdale rental?
faqs.a: It often helps. An HVHZ-compliant roof with proper deck attachment, documented roof-to-wall connections and impact-rated or protected openings can earn wind mitigation credits. A current panel, new supply lines and newer HVAC take care of the four-point side. We cannot predict any carrier's pricing, but we document every upgrade so your agent can present the strongest possible case to insurers at refinance and renewal.

faqs.q: Will an extra unit count in my Fort Lauderdale refinance?
faqs.a: Only if it is legally recognized. Many Fort Lauderdale duplexes and homes have informal extra units or converted garages that are not permitted. Appraisers and lenders generally exclude them, which can reduce the refinance value. We check permit history and zoning before purchase and price legalization when it is possible, so your refinance projection rests on units the appraiser will count.

rental-renovation.title: Rental Property Renovation in Fort Lauderdale | Genstone
rental-renovation.metaDescription: Fort Lauderdale rental renovations: humidity-proof portfolio standards, HVHZ roofs and openings, drain and concrete fixes, turns and occupied maintenance.
rental-renovation.h1: Rental Property Renovations in Fort Lauderdale
rental-renovation.intro: A Fort Lauderdale rental portfolio typically mixes mid-century block ranches west of the river, small duplexes in Poinsettia Heights or Middle River Terrace and a few older frame homes near Sailboat Bend or Croissant Park. They share the same enemies: humidity, salt air, cast-iron drains and flat roofs that hold water. Genstone renovates Fort Lauderdale rentals to a written portfolio standard designed for those conditions, so each house comes back from renovation with durable finishes, a dry roof, sound drains and an AC system that actually controls moisture. Genstone Field Services keeps the portfolio to that standard afterward with turns, occupied maintenance, inspections and code compliance, giving owners one accountable team across the city and the surrounding Broward communities.

sections.body:
The Fort Lauderdale standard starts with moisture. Floors are porcelain tile or polished original terrazzo, never carpet or laminate. Paint is mildew-resistant, with semi-gloss in kitchens and baths. Cabinets are built from materials that resist swelling, counters are solid surface or quartz and plumbing fixtures, hardware and appliances are standardized so property managers can stock parts.

Exterior items get equal attention. Door hardware, light fixtures, railings and fasteners are stainless or coated for corrosion resistance, especially east of US-1 and along the canals. Roofs are HVHZ-compliant, and flat roofs include tapered insulation so water drains instead of ponding.

Older frame homes near Sailboat Bend or Croissant Park may have original wood floors or details worth keeping, and those exceptions are documented in the standard. Over time, as more properties pass through renovation, the portfolio becomes more uniform and easier to maintain, appraise and sell. Owners who later sell a group of houses to a fund find that a documented, consistent standard makes the due diligence far simpler, because the buyer's inspector sees the same roof system, flooring and equipment at address after address.

Most maintenance calls in Fort Lauderdale rentals come from a short list of causes. Air conditioning failures and clogged condensate lines top the list, followed by roof leaks on flat roofs, cast-iron drain backups, leaking jalousie or awning windows and mold in bathrooms.

We address each during the renovation. HVAC systems are sized for the house and its humidity load, ducts are cleaned or replaced and condensate lines get proper traps and cleanouts. Flat roofs are replaced with HVHZ-compliant systems that drain properly. Drains are camera-inspected, and failing cast-iron lines are replaced before a tenant moves in. Old windows are replaced with impact-rated units or at least resealed.

Concrete gets attention as well. Spalling on tie beams, carport columns or exterior stairs worsens every year, and early repair costs far less than structural repair later. These items rarely show in listing photos, but they reduce emergency calls and lower the cost of every future turn.

sections.h2: Turns, storm prep and code compliance
sections.body:
Genstone Field Services handles Fort Lauderdale turns with the same specification used in the renovation: paint, flooring repairs, fixture replacement, appliance checks, AC service with condensate line cleaning, pest treatment and cleaning. For occupied homes, we coordinate maintenance with tenants and document conditions before and after.

Storm preparation fits naturally into the service. Before hurricane season, we can inspect roofs, drains, shutters and yard drainage and correct problems. After a storm or heavy rain event, we assess damage, secure properties and begin drying and repairs, with photos that support insurance claims.

Code officers in Fort Lauderdale and neighboring cities cite rentals for overgrown yards, debris, deteriorated exteriors and unpermitted structures, and those items are handled within the same service. Each visit produces photos and notes for deposit decisions, insurance and reporting, and invoices are itemized and approved after the work is complete.

For houses rented furnished or by the month, turns happen more often and the checklist grows to include linens, small appliances and a deeper clean. Fort Lauderdale requires vacation rentals to register with the city and meet its standards, and we keep those properties inspection-ready between guests.

faqs.q: What flooring works best in Fort Lauderdale rentals?
faqs.a: Porcelain tile and polished terrazzo. Both tolerate humidity, water and heavy use far better than laminate, wood or carpet. Many mid-century Fort Lauderdale homes have original terrazzo under later flooring, and polishing it can be cost-effective and attractive to tenants. Where terrazzo is missing or badly damaged, porcelain tile is our standard. Either choice also recovers well after a leak or minor flooding.

faqs.q: How do you reduce AC calls in Fort Lauderdale rentals?
faqs.a: We size systems for the house and its humidity load, clean or replace ducts and install condensate lines with proper traps and accessible cleanouts, since clogged lines are one of the most common causes of calls and ceiling damage. Bath fans are vented outdoors, and leaking windows and roofs are repaired so moisture does not enter walls. Each turn includes coil cleaning and a condensate line flush.

faqs.q: Can you manage turns and maintenance across Broward cities?
faqs.a: Yes. Many portfolios include homes in Fort Lauderdale, Wilton Manors, Oakland Park, Lauderhill and other Broward cities. Genstone Field Services handles turns, occupied maintenance, inspections and code compliance across those cities using the same portfolio standard. Each city has its own code enforcement and permitting, and we track requirements for each so owners have one process and one contact. That matters in central Broward, where a single street can cross a city line.

multifamily-renovation.title: Duplex & 2-4 Unit Renovation in Fort Lauderdale | Genstone
multifamily-renovation.metaDescription: Fort Lauderdale duplex and fourplex renovations: mid-century walk-ups, flat roofs, catwalk concrete, cast-iron drains, HVHZ openings and phased units.
multifamily-renovation.h1: Duplex and 2–4 Unit Renovations in Fort Lauderdale
multifamily-renovation.intro: The two-story walk-up with an exterior stair and catwalk is as much a Fort Lauderdale signature as the canal. Victoria Park, Poinsettia Heights, Middle River Terrace and Lake Ridge are full of them, along with side-by-side duplexes and small courtyard buildings from the 1950s and 1960s. They produce strong rents and draw steady investor interest, but they also share a predictable list of problems: flat roofs, cast-iron drains under the slab, spalling concrete on stairs and catwalks, jalousie windows and electrical services sized for a different era. Genstone renovates Fort Lauderdale duplexes, triplexes and fourplexes for investors and owner-occupants, working through structure, shared systems and HVHZ openings first, then unit interiors, and phasing the job so occupied units keep paying rent.

sections.h2: Fort Lauderdale's mid-century walk-ups and duplexes
sections.body:
Most Fort Lauderdale small multifamily was built of concrete block with concrete tie beams and slabs. Two-story walk-ups have exterior stairs and second-floor catwalks, often with metal railings. Side-by-side duplexes share a roof and a slab. Courtyard buildings arrange units around a central garden or pool.

The structure is usually sound, but exposed concrete elements deteriorate. Catwalks, stairs, balconies and tie beams show spalling where rebar has corroded, especially closer to the ocean and the Intracoastal. These repairs are structural and must be completed and permitted, sometimes with an engineer's design.

Unit counts deserve scrutiny. Many buildings have informal extra units, converted laundry rooms or garage apartments that are not recognized by the city. Before renovating, we compare permit records and zoning with the actual layout. That determines which units can be legally rented, financed and counted in a refinance appraisal, and whether any informal units should be legalized or removed.

Shared systems drive the budget on most Fort Lauderdale multifamily projects. Flat roofs often need full replacement with HVHZ-compliant systems and tapered insulation to eliminate ponding. Cast-iron drains under the slab may serve several units, so replacement requires careful planning. Older electrical services may need upgrades to support modern HVAC and appliances in each unit.

Many walk-ups already have separate electric meters, but panels and wiring inside each unit may be outdated. Where meters are shared, we evaluate separation with the utility.

Windows and doors are a major cost because walk-ups and courtyard buildings have many openings. Replacements must meet High-Velocity Hurricane Zone requirements. Impact-rated windows improve insurance credits, security and tenant comfort, while approved shutters may be more economical for some buildings.

Life-safety items include code-compliant railings on stairs and catwalks, fire separation between units, egress windows and smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Inspectors, insurers and lenders all look for these items on a walk-up, and none of them will sign off without the railings.

sections.h2: Phasing work in occupied Fort Lauderdale buildings
sections.body:
Fort Lauderdale multifamily buildings usually change hands with tenants in place. We plan work so rent continues. Vacant units are renovated first, while roofing, drain and electrical work that affects everyone is announced in advance and scheduled to keep disruptions short. Occupied units are renovated at turnover or around the household.

Concrete repair on stairs and catwalks requires special care. On many walk-ups, the upper units have only one route in, so repairs are completed in sections with shoring or temporary access, never leaving an occupied unit without a safe path.

Roof replacement is usually done in a single phase during the drier months. Window replacement can proceed unit by unit. Drain replacement may require temporary plumbing arrangements for affected units.

Your field manager keeps a unit-by-unit record of completed and planned work, supporting lender draws, refinance appraisals and leasing plans. Larger buildings may also fall under Broward County's building safety inspection program, which we review during scoping.

faqs.q: Is catwalk and stair spalling a big concern in Fort Lauderdale walk-ups?
faqs.a: It can be. Corroding rebar cracks the concrete on exterior stairs, catwalks and balconies, and left alone it becomes a safety issue. Repairs involve removing damaged concrete, treating or replacing the steel and patching to specification, usually with permits and sometimes an engineer's design. We evaluate this during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review so the cost is part of your budget before you buy.

faqs.q: Can you renovate a Victoria Park fourplex with tenants in place?
faqs.a: Yes. We renovate vacant units first, schedule roofing, drain and electrical work with notice and complete occupied units around tenants or at turnover. Concrete repair on stairs and catwalks is done in sections so occupied units always have safe access. This approach keeps rent coming while the building improves, and your field manager keeps a clear record of each unit's status.

faqs.q: Can I buy a Fort Lauderdale duplex with an FHA 203(k)?
faqs.a: Yes, if you live in one unit as your primary residence and the building has no more than four units. Structural concrete repairs and drain replacement under the slab often point toward the Standard 203(k) with a HUD consultant. Lighter scopes may fit the Limited program, which covers non-structural repairs up to $75,000. We prepare bids and scopes that meet lender and consultant requirements.

fha-203k.title: FHA 203(k) Contractor in Fort Lauderdale, FL | Genstone
fha-203k.metaDescription: FHA 203(k) certified contractor in Fort Lauderdale. Standard and Limited 203(k) bids for block homes and walk-up duplexes, HVHZ items, flood checks.
fha-203k.intro: For Fort Lauderdale buyers, an FHA 203(k) loan is often the only practical way into a house that needs an HVHZ roof, impact windows and a re-pipe before an insurer will cover it. The program puts the purchase and the renovation into one mortgage, and it lets owner-occupants buy a duplex or small walk-up of up to four units and live in one. Genstone is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor serving Fort Lauderdale and the surrounding Broward cities. We work with buyers, agents, lenders and HUD consultants to prepare bids that account for hurricane-code products, flat roofs, cast-iron drains and concrete repair, then manage the renovation through each draw to completion with a designated field manager.

sections.h2: Standard or Limited for Fort Lauderdale homes
sections.body:
A Limited 203(k), capped at $75,000, covers non-structural repairs without a HUD consultant. It often fits mid-century block ranches in Lauderdale Manors, Dorsey-Riverbend or west of I-95 that need an HVHZ roof, impact windows or shutters, a panel upgrade, re-piping, HVAC and kitchen and bath updates. These homes typically have sound structures, and the scope is predictable.

The Standard 203(k) requires a HUD-approved consultant and a $5,000 minimum repair amount, and it allows structural work. It is the better fit for walk-up duplexes with spalling on stairs and catwalks, homes needing tie beam or column repair and properties where additions must be rebuilt or legalized. Drain replacement requiring significant slab work may also push a project toward the Standard program.

We help buyers and lenders determine the right program early. HVHZ products can make Fort Lauderdale scopes larger than buyers expect, and discovering structural issues after the appraisal causes delays.

sections.h2: Fort Lauderdale properties that fit the program
sections.body:
Good Fort Lauderdale 203(k) candidates have sound structure, acceptable flood exposure and clear repair needs. Mid-century block ranches with older roofs, original windows, outdated electrical and cast-iron drains are common examples. Renovated comparables nearby help the appraiser support the improved value.

Duplexes and small walk-ups in Poinsettia Heights, Middle River Terrace and Lake Ridge are popular with owner-occupants who want rental income. These projects often require roofing, concrete repair, drain replacement and HVHZ openings, usually through the Standard program.

Some properties need extra caution. Homes in Special Flood Hazard Areas require flood insurance, and large scopes may reach the substantial improvement threshold. Properties that flooded in 2023 should be checked for incomplete remediation. Unpermitted additions or informal units may need legalization or removal before the lender will proceed. Condominiums generally do not fit the program well. We identify these issues during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review so buyers and agents can decide early.

sections.h2: Bids, draws and permits in Fort Lauderdale
sections.body:
A 203(k) project depends on clear, accurate bids. We itemize labor and materials by trade and location, include HVHZ product approvals and align the bid with the consultant's write-up on Standard loans. A draw schedule gives the lender a clear path to fund the work.

During construction, the lender releases funds as milestones are verified. Above the $15,000 inspection threshold, inspections occur before draws, so we organize work into stages that are easy to confirm, such as roof complete, windows installed and inspected or drains replaced. Your field manager sends photo updates to the buyer, agent and lender at each stage.

Permits come from the City of Fort Lauderdale or the relevant Broward city. We handle applications, product approvals, inspections, Notice of Commencement recording and lien waivers, and we close every permit we open.

At completion, the buyer receives documentation of the work and a one-year workmanship warranty. That file also supports the homeowner's insurance application.

faqs.q: Can a Fort Lauderdale 203(k) cover impact windows and a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes. Both are eligible repairs, and in Broward they must meet High-Velocity Hurricane Zone requirements. Depending on the overall scope, they can fit within the Limited program or form part of a larger Standard project. Because a house may have many openings and a flat roof may need tapered insulation, these items can be a large share of the budget, so we price them carefully.

faqs.q: Can I use a 203(k) on a walk-up duplex in Poinsettia Heights?
faqs.a: Yes, if the building has no more than four units and you live in one. Walk-ups often need concrete repair on stairs and catwalks, a new flat roof, drain replacement and HVHZ openings. Structural concrete work usually calls for the Standard program with a HUD consultant. We confirm the legal unit count first, then prepare the bid and coordinate with the consultant and lender.

faqs.q: Does flood history matter for a Fort Lauderdale 203(k)?
faqs.a: It does. Properties in Special Flood Hazard Areas require flood insurance, and a large scope may reach the substantial improvement threshold. Homes that flooded in 2023 may have hidden damage or incomplete remediation. We check flood zone and history during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review so the buyer, agent and lender understand the risks before the appraisal and can size the scope accordingly.

reo-renovation.title: REO & Bank-Owned Renovation in Fort Lauderdale | Genstone
reo-renovation.metaDescription: Fort Lauderdale REO renovation for servicers, banks and GSEs: flood-exposed homes, mold, flat roofs, unpermitted units, code cases, documented scopes.
reo-renovation.h1: REO and Bank-Owned Property Renovation in Fort Lauderdale
reo-renovation.intro: Bank-owned houses in Fort Lauderdale tend to fail from the top and the bottom at once. Flat roofs left unmaintained start leaking into block walls and ceilings, while cast-iron drains under the slab crack and back up the first time water is turned on. In between, a closed house with no air conditioning grows mold, an untreated pool draws mosquitoes and code officers, and an unpermitted back unit becomes a problem for every future buyer. Genstone renovates REO and bank-owned property across Fort Lauderdale and Broward County for mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and Government-Sponsored Enterprises, for which we are a preferred contractor. Genstone Field Services secures and stabilizes each property, and a designated field manager carries the file through scoping and renovation.

sections.body:
Roof failure is a leading cause of damage in vacant Fort Lauderdale homes. Flat and low-slope roofs need regular maintenance, and without it they pond, crack and leak into ceilings and walls. Interior damage can spread for months before anyone notices.

Mold follows any water intrusion and grows quickly in closed houses without air conditioning. Drywall, cabinets and ductwork often need remediation or replacement, guided by moisture readings.

Plumbing presents a delayed risk. Cast-iron drains under slabs may be cracked or broken, and turning water back on without testing can flood the house. We camera-inspect drains before restoring service.

Pools are another early priority. Untreated pools become breeding grounds for mosquitoes and draw code enforcement. Draining, cleaning and securing them is part of stabilization.

Flood-exposed homes, including those affected in 2023, may have hidden damage below the water line. Unpermitted additions and informal units affect valuation and disposition. We document all of these conditions at intake.

The first visits focus on stopping further deterioration. Genstone Field Services secures doors and windows, removes debris, cuts yards, treats or drains pools, tarps or patches roofs where needed and photographs every room. That gives the asset manager a baseline and reduces new code violations.

Our estimators then walk the property and prepare scope options with labor, materials and a draw schedule. Typically, one option covers the minimum work needed for an FHA or conventional buyer to finance and insure the property, and another covers a fuller renovation priced against renovated sales nearby. Comparing those options with an as-is investor offer helps the asset manager choose the best path.

Fort Lauderdale estimates account for HVHZ roofing and openings, cast-iron drain replacement, concrete spalling, unpermitted space, flood zone limits, four-point and wind mitigation items and permitting through the city or another Broward jurisdiction. Hauling and dumpsters are already inside the estimate, and each draw corresponds to a finished, photographed stage.

sections.h2: Records, code cases and vendor compliance
sections.body:
Institutional owners receive a complete file for each Fort Lauderdale property: intake, progress and completion photos, the approved scope and change log, permits and inspection results, product approvals for roofing and openings and signed lien waivers from every trade and supplier.

Code enforcement in Fort Lauderdale and neighboring cities commonly cites vacant properties for overgrown yards, debris, stagnant pools, unsecured structures and deteriorated exteriors. Some cities in Broward also require registration of vacant or foreclosed properties, and we can help keep properties in compliance with maintenance standards. We address active violations and coordinate with city staff until each case is closed.

Vendor compliance stays with us. Broward trades on Genstone jobs are vetted, licensed and insured, and we track their records. One field manager answers for each address, progress is visible without site visits and invoices are itemized against completed work, with the final payment held until the job is complete and approved.

faqs.q: Why test drains before restoring water to a Fort Lauderdale REO?
faqs.a: Because cast-iron drains under the slab are often cracked or broken in older Fort Lauderdale homes. Turning water back on and running fixtures can send wastewater into the soil beneath the slab or back up into the house. We camera-inspect the drains first, identify failures and include replacement in the scope where needed. That prevents new damage and gives the asset manager an accurate picture of plumbing costs.

faqs.q: Can you resolve code violations on a Fort Lauderdale bank-owned home?
faqs.a: Yes. Common citations include overgrown yards, debris, stagnant pools, unsecured buildings and deteriorated exteriors. Genstone Field Services handles immediate items during stabilization, and our renovation scope covers repairs required to close remaining cases. We stay in contact with city code staff until each case is formally closed, so violations do not delay the sale or affect financing. If the property sits in Wilton Manors or Oakland Park instead, we work with that city's officers the same way.

faqs.q: Do you work with GSEs and servicers in Broward County?
faqs.a: Yes. Government-Sponsored Enterprises count Genstone among their preferred contractors, and our institutional clients also include mortgage servicers, banks, REITs and investment funds. From Fort Lauderdale west to the edge of the Everglades and north to Pompano Beach, we handle preservation, inspections, repair scopes and complete renovations. Each property has one field manager, and the documentation package includes permits, HVHZ product approvals, lien waivers and vendor compliance records.
